label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: logs COMPLETE, timings COMPLETE, handler max 1210.116 ms, failures 0

A.rule: throughput shortfall without a slow consumer component

report.summary: Outbox publication fell behind arrivals, so notifications are delayed. Deliveries slowed mid-window because the consumer handler took about 1.2 s on some attempts. A stuck FAILED backlog also exists, and why the handler is slow is not shown.

findings.claim: Publications lagged arrivals: 670 committed vs 516 published (154 gap); publication rate dropped to ~7-8 per 10 s buckets while arrivals stayed at 30.
findings.reason: Per-bucket counts show publications collapsing mid-window while arrivals held steady, and pending grew from 1 to 166.

findings.claim: Slow deliveries come from the consumer handler (p95 1207 ms) while auth is ~70 ms and LedgerCore overhead is ~1 ms; all attempts succeeded.
findings.reason: The p95 total of 1279 ms is almost entirely consumer handler time; delivery logs show only 200 successes, with no errors.

findings.claim: The publication slowdown most likely follows from the slow consumer handler, since a poll batch of 20 delivered serially at ~1.2 s each cannot keep up with 30 arrivals per 10 s.
findings.reason: Config shows a 1 s poll and a batch size of 20; the throughput drop matches the slow handler timing, but no direct link by timestamp was captured.

findings.claim: The API and DB are not the bottleneck. Transfers return 201 with a p99 of 0.25 s, the pool has no waits or timeouts, and there is no DB blocking.
findings.reason: All three sources show healthy values across the window.

limitations: The handler latency by time bucket was not shown, so the correlation between slow handlers and the publication drop at ~06:39:40 is not confirmed.
The consumer is a test fixture, so its slow handler may not reflect production; the cause of the slowness is unknown.
next_checks: Break down consumer handler latency per 10 s bucket and compare with publication drops starting around 06:39:40.
Inspect the consumer fixture and the poller for serial delivery or sleeps, and explain the 531 vs 517 attempt discrepancy.

alternatives.reason: The failed count stayed constant at 1034 and oldest_undelivered_age is large and unchanged in kind, so it is not growing during the window.
alternatives.hypothesis: The old FAILED backlog (1034 rows, oldest age ~46,500 s) is a separate pre-existing issue, not the cause of the current delay.

alternatives.reason: Attempt records (517) differ from poll-batch-reported attempts (531), and no poller-side timing was collected.
alternatives.hypothesis: The outbox poller itself is stalled or throttled, independent of consumer latency.
